1: <!-- mcp-name: io.github.iPAYX-Technologies/mcp-fx-audit -->
2: # iPayX FX Audit MCP
3: **Expose hidden bank FX fees in 30 seconds. No signup required.**
4: A Model Context Protocol server for foreign exchange forensic auditing. Any AI agent (Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Cursor, Copilot) can check live mid-market rates, audit FX transactions against the mid-market rate in real time, and generate a full forensic report.
5: [![MCP Registry](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP%20Registry-Published-blue)](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io)
6: **Live endpoint:** `https://mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp`
7: **Server version:** 1.4.0 — remote, streamable HTTP, no install required.
8: ---
9: ## Tools
10: ### `check_fx_mid_market_rate`
11: Returns the live mid-market FX rate for a currency pair (Twelve Data, Open Exchange Rates fallback), in both directions. When `bank_rate` is given, the output also includes the spread versus mid-market.
12: **Parameters:**
13: - `currency_from` (string, required) - ISO 4217 base currency (e.g. `USD`)
14: - `currency_to` (string, required) - ISO 4217 quote currency (e.g. `CAD`)
15: - `bank_rate` (number, optional) - Bank/broker rate to compare against mid-market
16: **Auth:** None | **Cost:** Free
17: **Example:**
18: ```json
19: { "currency_from": "USD", "currency_to": "CAD" }
20: ```
21: ---
22: ### `audit_fx_transaction`
23: Audits one currency transaction against the live mid-market rate. Returns an FX score from 1 to 10, a rating, a verdict, the currency pair, amount and date.
24: **Parameters:**
25: - `amount` (number, required) - Transaction amount in `currency_from`
26: - `currency_from` (string, required) - ISO 4217 source currency
27: - `currency_to` (string, required) - ISO 4217 target currency
28: - `bank_rate` (number, required) - Rate the bank/broker actually charged
29: - `language` (string, optional) - `en` or `fr`
30: **Auth:** None | **Cost:** 3 free audits per IP per calendar month
31: **Example:**
32: ```json
33: {
34: "amount": 50000,
35: "currency_from": "USD",
36: "currency_to": "CAD",
37: "bank_rate": 1.3750
38: }
39: ```
40: ---
41: ### `compare_fx_sources`
42: Compares FX rates side by side: live mid-market, the Stripe FX Quotes API (when `stripe_api_key` is given) and the bank rate. Returns each source's effective rate, markup in basis points, cost per 100,000, FX score, and the lowest-cost source.
43: **Parameters:**
44: - `amount` (number, required) - Transaction amount
45: - `currency_from` (string, required) - Source currency (ISO 4217)
46: - `currency_to` (string, required) - Target currency (ISO 4217)
47: - `bank_rate` (number, required) - Rate quoted by the user's bank
48: - `bank_name` (string, optional) - Name of the bank (e.g. BMO, RBC, Chase)
49: - `stripe_api_key` (string, optional) - Stripe secret key to fetch a live FX quote
50: **Auth:** None | **Cost:** Free
51: **Example:**
52: ```json
53: { "amount": 100000, "currency_from": "USD", "currency_to": "CAD", "bank_rate": 1.3750 }
54: ```
55: ---
56: ### `full_forensic_fx_report`
57: Produces a full FX audit report for one transaction: score, spread, estimated loss, breakdown and routing recommendation.
58: **Parameters:**
59: - `amount` (number, required)
60: - `currency_from` (string, required)
61: - `currency_to` (string, required)
62: - `bank_rate` (number, required)
63: - `company_name` (string, optional) - Company name for the report
64: **Auth:** Bearer <redacted> — API key from https://www.ipayx.ai/ai-access
65: ---
66: ## Quick Start
67: ### Claude Desktop / Claude (custom connector)
68: Add a remote connector with the URL:
69: ```
70: https://mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp
71: ```
72: ### Cursor / Windsurf
73: ```json
74: {
75: "mcpServers": {
76: "ipayx-fx": {
77: "url": "https://mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp",
78: "transport": "streamable-http"
79: }
80: }
81: }
82: ```
83: ### Perplexity
84: Settings → Connectors → Add remote MCP server → paste URL:
85: ```
86: https://mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp
87: ```
88: ---
89: ## Score Interpretation
90: | Score | Meaning | Action |
91: |-------|---------|--------|
92: | 8-10 | Fair rate | No action needed |
93: | 5-7 | Moderate markup | Negotiate with bank |
94: | 1-4 | Excessive hidden fees | Request forensic report |
95: ---
96: ## Compliance
97: - **Operator:** iPayX (11850091 Canada Inc. operating as iPayX Protocol)
98: - **FINTRAC MSB:** C10001283
99: - **Jurisdiction:** Canada
100: - **FX Data Sources:** Twelve Data (primary) → Open Exchange Rates (fallback)
101: - **Read-only:** the server never moves money and never executes transfers. Audit information only — not financial advice.
102: ---
103: ## About iPayX Protocol
104: iPayX Protocol (11850091 Canada Inc.) is a rail-agnostic FX forensic audit layer for B2B payments. We audit hidden costs regardless of payment rail — SWIFT, SEPA or card.
105: **Website:** [www.ipayx.ai](https://www.ipayx.ai) | **API access:** [ipayx.ai/ai-access](https://www.ipayx.ai/ai-access)

29: Can you give me an API key?
30: The Xero API does not support basic API Key authentication. Our API uses OAuth 2.0 which means you need to register your app to get a client id and client secret which you use to access the API.
31: How can I try out the API?
32: The quickest way to try out the API is to set up your demo company and dive into the API Explorer. Most of the API functionality is supported and you can quickly start playing with real calls against demo data.
33: How do I connect Xero to my Salesforce/SQL Database/thing you have no SDK for?
34: We've got SDKs to cover the most used technologies in the community, but we'll never cater for everyone. If we don't support your particular tech then check out our developer forum archive, or connect with other developers on Stack Overflow. You can also use our OpenAPI spec to generate your own SDK.
35: How do I get a Xero account to develop/test against?
36: The first step is to sign up for a free Xero account. Once you have done that, you have two options as to how you can begin development without incurring any cost:
37: Use the demo company (recommended)
38: Start a trial or paid Xero organisation subscription
39: Check out our Development Accounts guide for more details.
40: How do I get support for building my integration?
41: Hopefully everything you need to know is on the Xero Developer Centre, but if you're still stuck we encourage you to connect with other developers on Stack Overflow, or engage with a Xero certified developer for hire.
42: What are some best practices for building an integration?
43: For some of the basics check out our Integration Best Practices guide. After that, browse through the rest of our how-to guides to find more guidance specific to your integration.
44: What Authentication do you support?
45: We currently support OAuth 1.0a and OAuth 2.0. However, OAuth 1.0a is in the process of being deprecated and OAuth 2.0 is required for all new integrations.
46: What kind of App should I build?
47: That's really up to you! Get connected with accountants and business owners to find out how you can help them be successful.

1: # xero-node 2: [![npm version](https://badge.fury.io/js/xero-node.svg)](https://badge.fury.io/js/xero-node) 3: [![Github forks](https://img.shields.io/github/forks/XeroAPI/xero-node.svg)](https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-node/network) 4: [![Github stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/XeroAPI/xero-node.svg)](https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-node/stargazers) 5: ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/xero-node) 6: The xero-node SDK makes it easy for developers to access Xero's APIs in their JavaScript code, and build robust applications and software using small business & general ledger accounting data. 7: # Table of Contents 8: - [API Client documentation](#api-client-documentation) 9: - [Sample Applications](#sample-applications) 10: - [Xero Account Requirements](#xero-account-requirements) 11: - [Installation](#installation) 12: - [Configuration](#configuration) 13: - [Authentication](#authentication) 14: - [Custom Connections](#custom-connections) 15: - [App Store Subscriptions](#app-store-subscriptions) 16: - [API Clients](#api-clients) 17: - [Helper Methods](#helper-methods) 18: - [Usage Examples](#usage-examples) 19: - [SDK conventions](#sdk-conventions) 20: - [Security](#security) 21: - [Contributing](#contributing) 22:
23: ## API Client documentation 24: This SDK supports full method coverage for the following Xero API sets: 25: | API Set | Description | 26: | --- | --- | 27: | [`Accounting`](https://xeroapi.github.io/xero-node/accounting/index.html) | The Accounting API exposes accounting functions of the main Xero application *(most commonly used)* 28: | [Assets](https://xeroapi.github.io/xero-node/assets/index.html) | The Assets API exposes fixed asset related functions of the Xero Accounting application | 29: | [Bankfeeds](https://xeroapi.github.io/xero-node/bankfeeds/index.html) | The Bankfeeds API facilitates the flow of transaction and statement data | 30: | [Files](https://xeroapi.github.io/xero-node/files/index.html) | The Files API provides access to the files, folders, and the association of files within a Xero organisation | 31: | [Projects](https://xeroapi.github.io/xero-node/projects/index.html) | Xero Projects allows businesses to track time and costs on projects/jobs and report on profitability | 32: | [Payroll (AU)](https://xeroapi.github.io/xero-node/payroll-au/index.html) | The (AU) Payroll API exposes payroll related functions of the payroll Xero application | 33: | [Payroll (NZ)](https://xeroapi.github.io/xero-node/payroll-nz/index.html) | The (NZ) Payroll API exposes payroll related functions of the payroll Xero application | 34: | [Payroll (UK)](https://xeroapi.github.io/xero-node/payroll-uk/index.html) | The (UK) Payroll API exposes payroll related functions of the payroll Xero application | 35: 36:
37: ## Sample Applications 38: Sample apps can get you started quickly with simple auth flows and advanced usage examples. 39: | Sample App | Description | Screenshot | 40: | --- | --- | --- | 41: | [`starter-app`](https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-node-oauth2-ts-starter) | Basic getting started code samples | 42: | [`full-app`](https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-node-oauth2-app) | Complete app with more complex examples | 43: | [`custom-connections-starter`](https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-node-custom-connections-starter) | Basic app showing Custom Connections - a Xero [premium option](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/custom-connections) for building M2M integrations to a single org | 44: | [`xero-node-sso-app`](https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-node-sso-app) | App showing Xero Single Sign On - as well as basic setup and usage of the Xero App Store `appStoreApi.getSubscription` endpoint | 45: | [`xero-node-sso-form`](https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-node-sso-form) | App showing Sign up with Xero to Lead | 46:
47: ## Xero Account Requirements 48: - Create a [free Xero user account](https://www.xero.com/us/signup/api/) 49: - Login to your Xero developer [dashboard](https://developer.xero.com/app/manage) and create an API application 50: - Copy the credentials from your API app and store them using a secure ENV variable strategy 51: - Decide the [neccesary scopes](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/oauth2/scopes) for your app's functionality 52: # Installation 53: To install this SDK in your project: 54: ``` 55: npm install xero-node 56: ``` 57: --- 58: ## Configuration 59: ```js 60: import { XeroClient } from 'xero-node'; 61: const xero = new XeroClient({ 62: clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID', 63: clientSecret: 'YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET', 64: redirectUris: [`http://localhost:${port}/callback`], 65: scopes: 'openid profile email accounting.settings accounting.transactions offline_access'.split(" "), 66: state: 'returnPage=my-sweet-dashboard', // custom params (optional) 67: httpTimeout: 3000, // ms (optional) 68: clockTolerance: 10 // seconds (optional) 69: }); 70: ``` 71: --- 72: ## Authentication 73: All API requests go through Xero's OAuth2.0 gateway and require a valid `access_token` to be set on the `client` which appends the `access_token` [JWT](https://jwt.io/) to the header of each request. 74: If you are making an API call for the first time: 75: 1. Send the user to the Xero authorization URL 76: ```js 77: let consentUrl = await xero.buildConsentUrl(); 78: res.redirect(consentUrl); 79: ``` 80: 2. The user will authorize your application and be sent to your `redirect_uri` 81: ```js 82: process.env.REDIRECT_URI 83: => /callback?code=xyz123 84: ``` 85: 3. You exchange the temporary `code` for a valid `token_set` 86: ```js 87: const tokenSet = await xero.apiCallback(req.url); 88: // save the tokenSet 89: ``` 90: It is recommended that you store this token set JSON in a datastore in relation to the user who has authenticated the Xero API connection. Each time you want to call the Xero API, you will need to access the previously generated token set, initialize it on the SDK `client`, and refresh the `access_token` prior to making API calls. 91: ### Token Set 92: | key | value | description | 93: | --- | --- | --- | 94: | id_token: | "xxx.yyy.zzz" | [OpenID Connect](https://openid.net/connect/) token returned if `openid profile email` scopes accepted | 95: | access_token: | "xxx.yyy.zzz" | [Bearer token](https://oauth.net/2/jwt/) with a 30 minute expiration required for all API calls | 96: | expires_in: | 1800 | Time in seconds till the token expires - 1800s is 30m | 97: | refresh_token: | "XXXXXXX" | Alphanumeric string used to obtain a new Token Set w/ a fresh access_token - 60 day expiry | 98: | scope: | ["email", "profile", "openid", "accounting.settings", "accounting.transactions", "offline_access"] | The Xero permissions that are embedded in the `access_token` | 99: Example Token Set JSON: 100: ``` 101: { 102: "id_token": "xxx.yyy.zz", 103: "access_token": "xxx.yyy.zzz", 104: "expires_in": 1800, 105: "token_type": "Bearer", 106: "refresh_token": "xxxxxxxxx", 107: "scope": ["email", "profile", "openid", "accounting.settings", "accounting.transactions", "offline_access"] 108: } 109: ``` 110: --- 111: ## Custom Connections 112: Custom Connections are a Xero [premium option](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/oauth2/custom-connections) used for building M2M integrations to a single organisation. A custom connection uses OAuth2.0's [`client_credentials`](https://www.oauth.com/oauth2-servers/access-tokens/client-credentials/) grant which eliminates the step of exchanging the temporary code for a token set. 113: To use this SDK with a `Custom Connection`: 114: ```js 115: import { XeroClient } from 'xero-node'; 116: const xero = new XeroClient({ 117: clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID', 118: clientSecret: 'YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET', 119: grantType: 'client_credentials' 120: }); 121: const tokenSet = await xero.getClientCredentialsToken(); 122: // save the tokenSet 123: const invoices = await xero.accountingApi.getInvoices(''); 124: ``` 125: Because Custom Connections are only valid for a single organisation you don't need to pass the `xero-tenant-id` as the first parameter to every method, or more specifically for this SDK `xeroTenantId` can be an empty string. 126: > Becuase the SDK is generated from the OpenAPI spec the parameter remains which requires you to pass an empty string to use this SDK with a Custom Connection. 127: --- 128: ## App Store Subscriptions 129: If you are implementing subscriptions to participate in Xero's App Store you will need to setup [App Store subscriptions](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/xero-app-store/app-partner-guides/xero-app-store-subscriptions) endpoints. 130: When a plan is successfully purchased, the user is redirected back to the URL specified in the setup process. The Xero App Store appends the subscription Id to this URL so you can immediately determine what plan the user has subscribed to through the subscriptions API. 131: With your app credentials you can create a client via `client_credentials` grant_type with the `marketplace.billing` scope. This unique access_token will allow you to query any functions in `appStoreApi`. Client Credentials tokens to query app store endpoints will only work for apps that have completed the App Store on-boarding process. 132: ```ts 133: // => /post-purchase-url 134: const xeroAppStoreClient = new XeroClient({ 135: clientId: process.env.CLIENT_ID, 136: clientSecret: process.env.CLIENT_SECRET, 137: grantType: 'client_credentials', 138: scopes: ['marketplace.billing'] 139: }); 140: try { 141: await xeroAppStoreClient.getClientCredentialsToken() 142: } catch(e) { 143: console.log('ERROR: ', e) 144: } 145: const subscriptionRequest = await xeroAppStoreClient.appStoreApi.getSubscription(subscripionId) 146: console.log(subscriptionRequest.body) 147: { 148: currentPeriodEnd: 2021-09-02T20:08:58.772Z, 149: endDate: null, 150: id: '03bc74f2-1237-4477-b782-2dfb1a6d8b21', 151: organisationId: '79e8b2e5-c63d-4dce-888f-e0f3e9eac647', 152: plans: [ 153: { 154: id: '6abc26f3-9390-4194-8b25-ce8b9942fda9', 155: name: 'Small', 156: status: 'ACTIVE', 157: subscriptionItems: [ 158: endDate: null, 159: id: '834cff4c-b753-4de2-9e7a-3451e14fa17a', 160: price: { 161: id: '2310de92-c7c0-4bcb-b972-fb7612177bc7', 162: amount: 0.1, 163: currency: 'NZD' 164: }, 165: product: Product { 166: id: '9586421f-7325-4493-bac9-d93be06a6a38', 167: name: '', 168: type: 'FIXED' 169: }, 170: startDate: 2021-08-02T20:08:58.772Z, 171: testMode: true 172: ] 173: } 174: ], 175: startDate: 2021-08-02T20:08:58.772Z, 176: status: 'ACTIVE', 177: testMode: true 178: } 179: ``` 180: You should use the subscription data to provision user access/permissions to your application. 181: ### App Store Subscription Webhooks 182: In additon to a subscription Id being passed through the URL, when a purchase or an upgrade takes place you will be notified via a webhook. You can then use the subscription Id in the webhook payload to query the AppStore endpoints and determine what plan the user purchased, upgraded, downgraded or cancelled. 183: Refer to Xero's documenation to learn more about setting up and receiving webhooks or review [this blogpost](https://devblog.xero.com/keeping-your-integration-in-sync-implementing-xero-webhooks-using-node-express-and-ngrok-6d2976baac6d) explaing webhooks using xero-node sdk. 184: > https://developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/webhooks/overview/ 185: --- 186: ## API Clients 187: You can access the different API sets and their available methods through the following: 188: ```js 189: const xero = new XeroClient({ 190: clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID', // required 191: clientSecret: 'YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET', // required 192: redirectUris: [`http://localhost:${port}/callback`], // not used for client_credentials auth flow 193: grantType: 'client_credentials', // only used for client_credentials auth flow 194: scopes: 'openid profile email accounting.settings accounting.transactions offline_access'.split(" "), // not used for client_credentials auth flow 195: state: 'returnPage=my-sweet-dashboard', // custom params (optional), not used for client_credentials auth flow 196: httpTimeout: 3000, // ms (optional) 197: clockTolerance: 10 // seconds (optional) 198: }); 199: xero.accountingApi 200: xero.assetApi 201: xero.projectApi 202: xero.filesApi 203: xero.payrollAUApi 204: xero.payrollNZApi 205: xero.payrollUKApi 206: ``` 207: --- 208: ## Helper Methods 209: Once you have a valid Token Set in your datastore, the next time you want to call the Xero API simply initialize a new `client` and refresh the token set. There are two ways to refresh a token 210: ```js 211: // you can refresh the token using the fully initialized client leveraging openid-client 212: import { XeroClient } from 'xero-node'; 213: const xero = new XeroClient({ 214: clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID', 215: clientSecret: 'YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET', 216: redirectUris: [`http://localhost:${port}/callback`], 217: scopes: 'openid profile email accounting.settings accounting.transactions offline_access'.split(" ") 218: }); 219: await xero.initialize(); 220: const tokenSet = getTokenSetFromDatabase(userId); // example function name 221: await xero.setTokenSet(tokenSet); 222: if(tokenSet.expired()){ 223: const validTokenSet = await xero.refreshToken(); 224: // save the new tokenset 225: } 226: ``` 227: ```js 228: // or if you already generated a tokenSet and have a valid (< 60 days refresh token), 229: // you can initialize an empty client and refresh by passing the client, secret, and refresh_token 230: import { XeroClient } from 'xero-node'; 231: const tokenSet = getTokenSetFromDatabase(userId); // example function name 232: if(tokenSet.expired()){ 233: const xero = new XeroClient(); 234: const validTokenSet = await xero.refreshWithRefreshToken(client_id, client_secret, tokenSet.refresh_token) 235: // save the new tokenset 236: } 237: ``` 238: A full list of the SDK client's methods: 239: | method | description | 240: | --- | --- | 241: | client.`initialize` | Initializes the Xero Client with the provided configuration | 242: | client.`buildConsentUrl` | Returns a url concatenated from the provided redirect uri, scope, and the issuer ( Xero identity authorize url) | 243: | client.`apiCallback`(callbackUrl) | Leverages openid-client library to exchange temporary auth code for token set | 244: | client.`disconnect`(connectionId) | Removes an individual tenant connection by connection ID | 245: | client.`readTokenSet` | Returns token set currently set on the Xero Client | 246: | client.`setTokenSet`(tokenSet) | Sets a specified token set on the Xero Client | 247: | client.`refreshToken` | Leverages openid-client library to refresh token set currently set on the Xero Client and returns updated token set | 248: | client.`revokeToken` | Revokes a users refresh token and removes all their connections to your app | 249: | client.`formatMsDate`(dateString) | Takes a date string and returns it formatted as an MS Date | 250: | client.`refreshWithRefreshToken`(clientId, clientSecret, refreshToken) | Refresh a token set without leveraging openid-client | 251: | client.`getClientCredentialsToken` | Get a token set without user intervention via the client credentials grant type for custom connections only | 252: | client.`updateTenants`(fullOrgDetails: boolean = true) | GET request to the /connections endpoint. Accepts a boolean to indicate whether or not to also make a GET request to the /organisations endpoint and map full org data to each connection object prior to returning the array of connections | 253: --- 254: ## Usage Examples 255: ### Accounting API 256: ```js 257: import { XeroClient, HistoryRecords, Invoice } from 'xero-node'; 258: const xero = new XeroClient({ 259: clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID', 260: clientSecret: 'YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET', 261: redirectUris: [`http://localhost:${port}/callback`], 262: scopes: 'openid profile email accounting.settings accounting.transactions offline_access'.split(" ") 263: }); 264: await xero.initialize(); 265: const tokenSet = getTokenSetFromDatabase(userId); // example function name 266: await xero.setTokenSet(tokenSet); 267: if(tokenSet.expired()){ 268: const validTokenSet = await xero.refreshToken(); 269: // save the new tokenset 270: } 271: await xero.updateTenants(); 272: const activeTenantId = xero.tenants[0].tenantId; 273: // GET all Accounts 274: const getAccountsResponse = await xero.accountingApi.getAccounts(activeTenantId); 275: const accountId = getAccountsResponse.body.accounts[0].accountID 276: // GET one Account by ID 277: const getAccountResponse = await xero.accountingApi.getAccount(activeTenantId, accountId); 278: // CREATE an Invoice 279: const invoices = { 280: invoices: [ 281: { 282: type: Invoice.TypeEnum.ACCREC, 283: contact: { 284: contactID: contactId 285: }, 286: lineItems: [ 287: { 288: description: "Acme Tires", 289: quantity: 2.0, 290: unitAmount: 20.0, 291: accountCode: "500", 292: taxType: "NONE", 293: lineAmount: 40.0 294: } 295: ], 296: date: "2019-03-11", 297: dueDate: "2018-12-10", 298: reference: "Website Design", 299: status: Invoice.StatusEnum.AUTHORISED 300: } 301: ] 302: }; 303: const createdInvoicesResponse = await xero.accountingApi.createInvoices(activeTenantId, invoices) 304: const invoiceId = createdInvoicesResponse.body.invoices[0].invoiceID; 305: // CREATE a History Record 306: const historyRecords: HistoryRecords = { 307: historyRecords: [ 308: { 309: details: "This is a history record" 310: } 311: ] 312: }; 313: const createdInvoiceHistoryResponse = await xero.accountingApi.createInvoiceHistory(activeTenantId, invoiceId, historyRecords); 314: // CREATE Attachment 315: const filename = "xero-dev.png"; 316: const pathToUpload = path.resolve(__dirname, "../public/images/xero-dev.png"); 317: const readStream = fs.createReadStream(pathToUpload); 318: const contentType = mime.lookup(filename); 319: const accountAttachmentsResponse = await xero.accountingApi.createInvoiceAttachmentByFileName(activeTenantId, invoiceId, filename, readStream, { 320: headers: { 321: 'Content-Type': contentType 322: } 323: }); 324: ``` 325: --- 326: ## SDK conventions 327: ### Querying & Filtering 328: ```js 329: const activeTenantId = 'XERO_TENANT_ID'; 330: const ifModifiedSince: Date = new Date("2020-02-06T12:17:43.202-08:00"); 331: const where = 'Status=="AUTHORISED" AND Type=="SPEND"'; 332: const order = 'Reference ASC'; 333: const page = 1; 334: const unitdp = 4; 335: const response = await xero.accountingApi.getBankTransactions(activeTenantId, ifModifiedSince, where, order, page, unitdp); 336: ``` 337: Note that you should set the query param to undefined instead of null if you wish to ignore a specific filter. 338: ```js 339: const purchaseOrders = xero.accountingApi.getPurchaseOrders(tenant.tenantId, null, null, '2021-01-01', '2021-04-25', null, 1); 340: // http://api-oauth2.xero.com/api.xro/2.0/PurchaseOrders?Status=&DateFrom=2008-01-01&DateTo=2021-04-25&order=&page=1 341: // "Status=&" is breaking the above query 342: // purchaseOrders will be an empty array 343: const purchaseOrders = xero.accountingApi.getPurchaseOrders(tenant.tenantId, undefined, undefined, '2021-01-01', '2021-04-25', undefined, 1); 344: // http://api-oauth2.xero.com/api.xro/2.0/PurchaseOrders?DateFrom=2008-01-01&DateTo=2021-04-25&order=&page=1 345: // params are omitted 346: // purchaseOrders array will have results now 347: ``` 348: --- 349: ## Security 350: This repo leverages a certified OA2 and OIDC library called openid-client. For a deeper dive the repo's functionality, check out them directly https://github.com/panva/node-openid-client. 351: ### Preventing CSRF Using Xero-Node 352: When xero.buildConsentUrl is called we call openid-client authorizationUrl method, passing redirect_uri, scope, and state (if present) as arguments and returns a formatted url string made up from the given config. The user is then directed to the consentUrl to begin the auth process with Xero. When the auth process is complete Xero redirects the user to the specified callback route and passes along params including the state if it was initially provided. At this point openid-client takes over verifying params.state and check.state match if provided. If the state does not match the initial user's, the openid-client library throws an error: 353: ``` 354: RPError: state mismatch, expected user=1234, got: user=666 355: ``` 356: ### JWT Verification Using Xero-Node 357: JWT verification of both the `access_token` and `id_token` are baked into the openid-client library we leverage. When `xero.apiCallback` is called, openid-client `validateJARM` is triggered which also invokes `validateJWT`. If openid-client fails to validate the JWT signature it will throw an error. 358: --- 359: ## Contributing 360: PRs, issues, and discussion are highly appreciated and encouraged. Note that the majority of this project is generated code based on [Xero's OpenAPI specs](https://github.com/XeroAPI/Xero-OpenAPI) - PR's will be evaluated and pre-merge will be incorporated into the root generation templates. 361: Please add tests for net new functionality and ensure existing test suite passes all tests. 362: ``` 363: npm test 364: ``` 365: ### Versioning 366: We do our best to keep OS industry `semver` standards, but we can make mistakes! If something is not accurately reflected in a version's release notes please let the team know. 367: ## Participating in Xero’s developer community 368: This SDK is one of a number of SDK’s that the Xero Developer team builds and maintains. We are grateful for all the contributions that the community makes. 369: Here are a few things you should be aware of as a contributor: 370: * Xero has adopted the Contributor Covenant [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-node/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), we expect all contributors in our community to adhere to it 371: * If you raise an issue then please make sure to fill out the github issue template, doing so helps us help you 372: * You’re welcome to raise PRs. As our SDKs are generated we may use your code in the core SDK build instead of merging your code 373: * We have a [contribution guide](https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-node/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) for you to follow when contributing to this SDK 374: * Curious about how we generate our SDK’s? Have a [read of our process](https://devblog.xero.com/building-sdks-for-the-future-b79ff726dfd6) and have a look at our [OpenAPISpec](https://github.com/XeroAPI/Xero-OpenAPI) 375: * This software is published under the [MIT License](https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-node/blob/master/LICENSE) 376: For questions that aren’t related to SDKs please refer to our [developer support page](https://developer.xero.com/support/).

1: # Brex MCP
2: The Brex MCP server lets AI assistants interact directly with your Brex account: manage expenses, look up users, check cards, review banking transactions, track bills, and more through natural language.
3: Beta
4: The MCP server's tools may change as we continue developing new use cases and features.
5: ## Prerequisites
6: 1. **Accept the Developer API agreement.** An account admin or card admin must accept the Developer API agreement in **Settings → Developer**.
7: 2. **Enable the beta.** Go to **Settings → Beta features** in the Brex Dashboard and select **Brex in AI assistants**.
8: Once enabled, all users in your Brex account can connect to the MCP server with their own credentials. This is different from the Brex Developer API, which requires admin-provisioned API tokens. Any employee can authorize via OAuth and access tools based on their Brex capabilities. The Access column in the tools table below shows which capability each tool requires.
9: ## Connect to the Brex MCP server
10: The server is hosted at `https://api.brex.com/mcp` and supports any MCP-compatible client. Most clients handle authentication automatically with discovery. Just add the server URL and you'll be prompted to log in with your Brex account.
11: ### Claude Code
12: ```bash
13: claude mcp add --transport http brex https://api.brex.com/mcp
14: ```
15: Then verify the connection:
16: ```bash
17: claude /mcp
18: ```
19: ### Claude Desktop
20: Install the [Brex connector](https://claude.com/connectors/brex) from the Claude connectors directory.
21: Alternatively, add it manually to your config file:
22: - **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
23: - **Windows**: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`
24: ```json
25: {
26: "mcpServers": {
27: "brex": {
28: "command": "npx",
29: "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://api.brex.com/mcp"],
30: "env": {}
31: }
32: }
33: }
34: ```
35: Restart Claude Desktop after saving. Requires Node.js v20+.
36: ### ChatGPT
37: Install the [Brex app](https://chatgpt.com/apps/brex/asdk_app_6961bc9309ec819199ce7ce38b7d3bf1) from the ChatGPT app directory.
38: ### Cursor
39: Open **Settings → MCP** and add a new server:
40: - **Name**: `brex`
41: - **Type**: `http`
42: - **URL**: `https://api.brex.com/mcp`
43: ### Codex
44: ```bash
45: codex mcp add brex --url https://api.brex.com/mcp
46: ```
47: ### Other MCP clients
48: Any client that supports MCP HTTP transport can connect to `https://api.brex.com/mcp`. If your client supports OAuth with Dynamic Client Registration, authentication is handled automatically. Otherwise, use an API key (see below).
49: ## Authentication
50: The Brex MCP server supports two authentication methods.
51: ### OAuth (recommended)
52: MCP clients that support OAuth will automatically initiate a browser-based authorization flow when you first connect. No manual token setup required.
53: - **Authorization server**: `https://accounts-api.brex.com/oauth2/default`
54: - **Discovery endpoint**: `https://api.brex.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`
55: The server supports [Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591)](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7591), so MCP clients don't need to be pre-registered. Sessions remain active, so you won't need to re-authorize on every use.
56: You can view and revoke authorized sessions from **Settings → Personal settings → Connected integrations** in the Brex Dashboard.
57: ### API key
58: For clients that don't support OAuth, or for programmatic access, account and card admins can authenticate with a Brex API token. Generate one from **Settings → Developer** in the Brex Dashboard.
59: Pass it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header:
60: ```
61: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_BREX_ACCESS_TOKEN
62: ```
63: For example, in Claude Code:
64: ```bash
65: claude mcp add --transport http brex https://api.brex.com/mcp \
66: --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_BREX_ACCESS_TOKEN"
67: ```
68: Or in `.mcp.json`:
69: ```json
70: {
71: "mcpServers": {
72: "brex": {
73: "type": "http",
74: "url": "https://api.brex.com/mcp",
75: "headers": {
76: "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_BREX_ACCESS_TOKEN"
77: }
78: }
79: }
80: }
81: ```
82: ### Security best practices
83: - **Prefer OAuth over API keys.** OAuth scopes access to what you authorize, and sessions can be revoked from the Dashboard.
84: - **Use restricted tokens.** If using API keys, create tokens with only the scopes your use case needs.
85: - **Enable human confirmation.** Configure your AI assistant to require approval before executing actions.
86: - **Store tokens securely.** Use environment variables; never commit tokens to version control.
87: - **Monitor usage.** Review API logs in the Brex Dashboard to track MCP activity.
88: ## Available tools
89: Each tool requires a specific Brex capability. The Access column indicates which capability a user needs to call the tool. Your Brex permissions carry over; you only see and modify what you're authorized to. Actions like approvals and card management are not yet available via MCP.
90: Card data
91: Brex does not and will not expose raw card numbers (PANs), CVVs, or expiration dates over MCP. Card-related tools return only non-sensitive metadata such as card names, statuses, and limits.
92: | Tool Name | Description | Access |
93: | --- | --- | --- |
94: | `get_user_myself` | Get the current authenticated user. | All users |
95: | `get_user_by_id` | Get a user by their unique ID. | All users |
96: | `list_users_by_name_or_email` | List users by name or email. | All users |
97: | `list_users` | List users with optional filtering and pagination. | All users |
98: | `list_cost_centers` | List cost centers. | All users |
99: | `list_departments` | List departments. | All users |
100: | `list_locations` | List locations. | All users |
101: | `list_legal_entities` | List legal entities. | All users |
102: | `list_titles` | List employee titles. | All users |
103: | `list_roles` | List Brex account roles. | All users |
104: | `get_reward_points` | Get the Brex reward points balance and redemption eligibility for the authenticated account. | Users with view rewards capability |
105: | `list_expenses` | List expenses with comprehensive filtering. | Users with view expenses capability |
106: | `get_expense_by_id` | Get an expense by its ID. | Users with view expenses capability |
107: | `query_expense_analytics` (deprecated) | Ask high-level company spend questions. Use `brex-analytics` instead. | Account admin or Card admin |
108: | `brex-analytics` | Ask questions about your Brex accounts, including spend, banking, accounting, and more. | Account admin or Card admin |
109: | `update_expense_memo` | Update memo for multiple expenses in bulk. | All users |
110: | `upload_card_expense_receipt_from_urls` | Upload receipts to a card expense by downloading them from provided URLs. | All users |
111: | `replace_attendees_for_card_expense` | Update attendees for a card expense. | All users |
112: | `assign_limit_for_card_expenses` | Assign one or more card expenses to a spend limit. | All users |
113: | `get_reimbursement_payout_date` | Get the expected payout date for a reimbursement expense. | All users |
114: | `start_expense_download` | Start an asynchronous expense download job. | Users with view expenses capability |
115: | `get_expense_download_result` | Check the status of an expense download job and get the download URL when ready. | All users |
116: | `list_merchants` | Search card merchants by name. | All users |
117: | `list_merchant_categories` | List merchant categories (e.g., Restaurants, Software, Travel). | All users |
118: | `list_expense_categories` | List all available expense categories (also known as 'expense types' in Brex) for filtering expenses. | All users |
119: | `list_cards` | List cards with comprehensive filtering. | All users |
120: | `get_card_by_id` | Get a card by its ID. | Users with view cards and limits capability |
121: | `get_expense_policy` | Get expense policy information for a limit as structured, validatable content. | Users with view policy capability |
122: | `list_my_limits` | Get all spend limits that apply to the current user with pagination support. | All users |
123: | `list_business_accounts` | List business bank accounts. | Users with view accounts and balances capability |
124: | `get_business_account` | Get a business bank account by ID. | Users with view accounts and balances capability |
125: | `list_banking_transactions` | List banking transactions with filtering. | Users with view accounts and balances capability |
126: | `get_banking_transaction` | Get a banking transaction by ID. | Users with view accounts and balances capability |
127: | `list_bills` | List bills with filtering. | Users with view bills and vendors capability |
128: | `get_bill_by_id` | Get a bill by its ID. | Users with view bills and vendors capability |
129: | `get_vendor_by_id` | Get a vendor by ID. | Users with view bills and vendors capability |
130: | `list_vendors` | Get all vendors for the current authenticated user. | Users with view all bills/vendors capability |
131: | `get_active_integration` | Get the active accounting integration. | Users with manage accounting integration capability |
132: | `list_accounting_records` | List accounting records. | Users with view transactions capability |
133: | `list_gl_accounts` | List general ledger accounts. | Users with manage mappings, fields, and rules capability |
134: | `list_trips` | List travel trips across the company with filtering, sorting, and pagination. | Users with view travel capability |
135: | `list_bookings` | List travel bookings across the company with filtering, sorting, and pagination. | Users with view travel capability |
136: | `list_group_events` | List group travel events (company offsites, conferences, etc.) with filtering, sorting, and pagination. | Users with view travel capability |
137: | `submit_feedback` | Submit feedback about the Brex API or MCP tools to the Brex product team on behalf of the user. | All users |
138: ## Example prompts
139: Once connected, try these with your AI assistant:
140: **Expense review**
141: > "Show me all my expenses from the past month that are missing receipts."
142: **User lookup**
143: > "Find the user with email sarah@acme.com and show me their department and role."
144: **Spend analysis**
145: > "What are my current spend limits and how much budget do I have remaining?"
146: **Company spend (admin)**
147: > "What was our total spend on software last quarter?"
148: **Banking**
149: > "Show me the last 10 transactions on our primary business account."
150: **Travel**
151: > "List all upcoming trips booked for next month."
152: ## Troubleshooting
153: ### OAuth flow not completing
154: 1. Check that your browser allows popups from `accounts-api.brex.com`.
155: 2. Confirm the beta is enabled in **Settings → Beta features**.
156: 3. Try clearing your browser cookies for `accounts-api.brex.com` and reconnecting.
157: ### `401 Unauthorized`
158: 1. If using OAuth, your session may have expired. Reconnect to re-authorize.
159: 2. If using an API key, confirm the token includes the `Bearer` prefix.
160: 3. Generate a new token from **Settings → Developer** in the Brex Dashboard.
161: ### Tools not appearing
162: 1. Restart your AI assistant after adding the MCP server config.
163: 2. Check your assistant's logs for connection errors.
164: 3. Verify the JSON config has no syntax errors.
165: ### Connection timeouts
166: 1. Verify the URL is exactly `https://api.brex.com/mcp`.
167: 2. Check your network allows outbound HTTPS connections.
168: 3. If using `mcp-remote`, ensure Node.js v20+ is installed.
169: ## Resources
170: - [Model Context Protocol specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
171: - [Brex API documentation](/)
172: - [Brex API support](/docs/support)

1: title: Authorization
2: source_url: /developer-api/v1/authorization
3: summary: Ramp uses OAuth 2.0. Your app gets an access token from /developer/v1/token, authenticating with its client ID and secret (typically HTTP Basic Auth), and scopes control what the token can access.
4: content:
5: Ramp uses OAuth 2.0. Your app gets an access token from `/developer/v1/token`, authenticating with its client ID and secret (typically HTTP Basic Auth), and scopes control what the token can access.
6: For a quick start, see the [Setup Guide](</developer-api/v1/getting-started>). For Ramp's own MCP server and CLI, see [Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI](<#ramp-mcp-and-ramp-cli>).
7: ## Supported grant types
8: | Grant Type | Use Case | User Interaction |
9: | --- | --- | --- |
10: | **Client Credentials** | Internal integrations, server-to-server | None required |
11: | **Authorization Code** | Third-party apps, public integrations | Authorized user consent required |
12: | **Refresh Token** | Renew access after an Authorization Code grant | None after the initial authorization |
13: ## Permission model and scopes
14: Scopes follow the pattern `resource:permission`, where the permission is usually `read` or `write`, such as `transactions:read`. A few use other permissions, such as `cards:read_vault`. OpenID Connect scopes, such as `openid` and `offline_access`, don't follow the pattern.
15: Request only the scopes your app needs. Each endpoint's API reference lists its required scopes. The table below lists common scopes and isn't exhaustive.
16: | Scope | Resource | Description |
17: | --- | --- | --- |
18: | `accounting:read` | Accounting data | Access accounting sync status and metadata |
19: | `accounting:write` | Accounting data | Update accounting sync settings and connections |
20: | `ai_spend:read` | AI spend | View AI token usage and spend data |
21: | `ai_spend:write` | AI spend | Update AI spend and tagging settings |
22: | `ai_usage:write` | AI usage | Report AI and LLM usage data for spend tracking |
23: | `applications:read` | Applications | View financing application status (partners only) |
24: | `applications:write` | Applications | Requested in the application OAuth consent flow; not required to submit applications (partners only) |
25: | `approvals:read` | Approvals | View approval data for transactions, reimbursements, and bills |
26: | `approvals:write` | Approvals | Approve or reject pending approvals |
27: | `audit_logs:read` | Audit logs | View business audit log events |
28: | `bank_accounts:read` | Bank accounts | View connected bank account information |
29: | `bank_accounts:write` | Bank accounts | Create and manage bank account information (partners only) |
30: | `billing_statements:read` | Billing statements | View your Ramp billing statements |
31: | `bills:read` | Bills | Access bill data and payment history |
32: | `bills:write` | Bills | Create, update, and pay bills |
33: | `blank_canvas:write` | Blank canvas approvals | Approve, reject, and update external workflow steps |
34: | `budgets:read` | Budgets | View budget information |
35: | `business:read` | Business profile | Access business information and settings |
36: | `cards:read` | Cards | View physical and virtual card information |
37: | `cards:read_vault` | Card vault | Access sensitive card data (PAN, CVV) |
38: | `cards:write` | Cards | Create, update, and manage cards |
39: | `cashbacks:read` | Cashback rewards | View cashback earnings and history |
40: | `custom_forms:read` | Custom forms | View custom form collection responses |
41: | `custom_records:read` | Custom records | Access custom data fields and records |
42: | `custom_records:write` | Custom records | Create and update custom data fields |
43: | `departments:read` | Departments | View department structure and assignments |
44: | `departments:write` | Departments | Create and manage departments |
45: | `embedded_cards:write` | Embedded cards | View sensitive card details through Ramp Embedded |
46: | `entities:read` | Legal entities | Access entity information and hierarchies |
47: | `funds:read` | Funds | View funds, members, cards, and spending policies |
48: | `funds:write` | Funds | Create and manage funds, members, and suspension state |
49: | `incorporation:read` | Incorporation | View incorporation information and status (partners only) |
50: | `incorporation:write` | Incorporation | Submit and update incorporation information (partners only) |
51: | `item_receipts:read` | Item receipts | View itemized receipt data |
52: | `item_receipts:write` | Item receipts | Create and update itemized receipt data |
53: | `limits:write` | Card vault compatibility | Required with `cards:read_vault` when creating a card through `POST /developer/v1/cards/vault` |
54: | `locations:read` | Locations | View location data and assignments |
55: | `locations:write` | Locations | Create and manage location data |
56: | `memos:read` | Memos | Access transaction memos and notes |
57: | `memos:write` | Memos | Add and update transaction memos |
58: | `merchants:read` | Merchants | View merchant information and policies |
59: | `payments:read` | Payments | View vendor payments |
60: | `payments:write` | Payments | Create and initiate vendor payments |
61: | `purchase_orders:read` | Purchase orders | Access purchase order data and status |
62: | `purchase_orders:write` | Purchase orders | Create and update purchase orders |
63: | `receipt_integrations:read` | Receipt integrations | View receipt integration settings |
64: | `receipt_integrations:write` | Receipt integrations | Configure receipt integration settings |
65: | `receipts:read` | Receipts | Access receipt images and data |
66: | `receipts:write` | Receipts | Upload and manage receipt data |
67: | `reimbursements:read` | Reimbursements | View reimbursement requests and status |
68: | `reimbursements:write` | Reimbursements | Create and update reimbursement requests |
69: | `repayments:read` | Repayments | View repayments |
70: | `spend_programs:read` | Spend programs | Access spend program configuration |
71: | `spend_programs:write` | Spend programs | Create and manage spend programs |
72: | `spend_requests:write` | Spend requests | Create and update spend requests |
73: | `statements:read` | Statements | Download monthly statements |
74: | `tasks:read` | Tasks | View task information and status |
75: | `transactions:read` | Transactions | Access transaction data and history |
76: | `transactions:write` | Transactions | Update transaction data and accounting information |
77: | `transfers:read` | Transfers | View transfer history and status |
78: | `treasury:read` | Banking | View banking accounts and balance history |
79: | `trips:read` | Trips | View trips |
80: | `unified_requests:read` | Requests | View requests, such as procurement requests |
81: | `unified_requests:write` | Requests | Create, edit, and submit procurement requests |
82: | `users:read` | Users | Access user profiles and roles |
83: | `users:write` | Users | Create and manage user accounts |
84: | `vendors:read` | Vendors | View vendor information and payment details |
85: | `vendors:write` | Vendors | Create and update vendor information |
86: `cards:read_vault` is available only to approved integrators; see [Virtual Cards](</developer-api/v1/virtual-cards#vault-api>). Scopes marked partners only appear in the partner Developer Console, not in a business's own Developer API settings. Some endpoints also require a Ramp plan feature and return `403` without it, even with the right scope.
87: ## Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI
88: [Ramp MCP](</developer-api/v1/ramp-mcp>) and [Ramp CLI](</developer-api/v1/cli>) sign in with OAuth, but you don't choose scopes. A connection can do what the connecting user's Ramp role allows, within the access level chosen at sign-in.
89: When you connect, the consent screen asks you to choose **Full access** (the default) or **Read-only**. With the CLI, you can also run `ramp auth login --read-only`. A read-only connection gets read scopes only:
90: - Ramp MCP doesn't list tools that make changes.
91: - Write requests fail with `403 Forbidden` and error code `DEVELOPER_7100` (`These scopes are not allowed for this token: ...`). Through Ramp MCP, the agent sees this as a tool error.
92: To make changes, reconnect and choose **Full access**, or run `ramp auth login` without `--read-only`.
93: Unlike other apps, Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI get a new refresh token each time they refresh, and its lifetime restarts. Connections still expire 30 days after they're created; reconnect to renew. Who can connect is controlled by a Ramp role permission; see [Manage connected AI tools↗](<https://support.ramp.com/managing-connected-ai-tools>).
94: Third-party apps are unchanged: they get exactly the scopes they were granted.
95: ## Token management
96: - **Format**: Access tokens are bearer tokens prefixed with `ramp_business_tok_`, `ramp_user_tok_`, `ramp_business_jwt_`, or `ramp_user_jwt_`.
97: - **Lifetime**: Client Credentials access tokens last 10 days (864,000 seconds). Authorization Code and Refresh Token access tokens default to 1 hour (3,600 seconds), and some apps have a different configured lifetime. Use `expires_in` from the token response.
98: - **Scopes**: A token can't be used beyond its granted scopes. To change scopes, get a new token. Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI tokens are limited by the user's role and access level instead.
99: - **Environment**: Tokens work only in the environment that issued them. Sandbox and production need separate apps.
100: ## Treat tokens as credentials
101: Never log tokens or include them in error messages, store them encrypted, and send them only over HTTPS.
102: ## Authorization flows
103: ### Client credentials flow
104: Use this flow for server-to-server integrations with your own Ramp business. Send `client_id:client_secret`, base64-encoded, in an `Authorization: Basic ...` header. Some apps are configured to send `client_id` and `client_secret` in the form body instead.
105: Pass the scopes you need as a space-separated `scope` field. If you omit `scope`, the token has no scopes. The token has business-wide access limited by those scopes, and there's no end user. Actions that need a user are attributed to the app's creator by default.
106: Client Credentials doesn't return a refresh token. Request a new access token when the current one expires. Keep the client secret on your servers, never in client-side code.
107: ### Authorization code flow
108: Use this flow when other Ramp businesses or users grant your app access, such as apps listed on ramp.com/integrations.
109: #### Step 1: Redirect the user to Ramp
110: Send the user to Ramp's authorization URL with these parameters:
111: - `response_type` Required — Must be `code`.
112: - `scope` Required — Space-separated list of scopes, such as `transactions:read business:read`.
113: - `client_id` Required — Your app's client ID from the [Ramp Developer Console↗](<https://app.ramp.com/settings/ramp-developer>).
114: - `redirect_uri` Required — Must exactly match a redirect URI configured for your app, including the path. Use `https://`, or `http://` only for `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`.
115: - `state` Required — A random value your app verifies on return, to protect against CSRF. Required for apps created after June 15, 2023, and recommended for all apps.
116: ```text
117: https://app.ramp.com/v1/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=https://yourapp.com/callback&scope=transactions:read business:read&state=random_csrf_token
118: ```
119: Use the builder below to generate a correctly encoded URL. It uses `https://demo.ramp.com/v1/authorize` for sandbox and `https://app.ramp.com/v1/authorize` for production. No client secret is needed.
120: #### Step 2: The user approves access
121: The user signs in to Ramp and approves your app's requested access.
122: ## Who can approve
123: For apps that access the whole business, an Admin or Business Owner must approve. Other users see "An admin must connect this app." For apps that act as an individual user, an admin must first enable the app for the organization in **Manage Access**.
124: Ramp then redirects to your `redirect_uri` with a `code` and the original `state`. If the user denies access, the redirect includes `error=access_denied` instead.
125: ```text
126: https://yourapp.com/callback?code=AUTH_CODE_HERE&state=random_csrf_token
127: ```
128: #### Step 3: Exchange the code for an access token
129: Codes expire after 5 minutes.
130: ```bash
131: curl --request POST '{environment-url}/developer/v1/token' \
132: --header "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET" | base64)" \
133: --header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
134: --data-urlencode "grant_type=authorization_code" \
135: --data-urlencode "code=AUTH_CODE_HERE" \
136: --data-urlencode "redirect_uri=https://yourapp.com/callback"
137: ```
138: #### Step 4: Refresh the access token
139: To get refresh tokens, enable the Refresh Token grant type for your app. Then exchange the refresh token for a new access token:
140: ```bash
141: curl --request POST '{environment-url}/developer/v1/token' \
142: --header "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET" | base64)" \
143: --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
144: --data-urlencode 'grant_type=refresh_token' \
145: --data-urlencode 'refresh_token=REFRESH_TOKEN_HERE'
146: ```
147: The response has a new access token but no new refresh token. Keep using the original refresh token until it expires or is revoked, then restart the Authorization Code flow. `refresh_token_expires_in` is returned with the original refresh token only if your app has a configured refresh-token lifetime; refreshing doesn't extend it.
148: ### Revoke an access or refresh token
149: Send the token to `POST /developer/v1/token/revoke`, with the same Basic Auth credentials you use to create tokens. A successful request returns HTTP `200`.
150: ```bash
151: curl --request POST 'https://api.ramp.com/developer/v1/token/revoke' \
152: --header "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET" | base64)" \
153: --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
154: --data-urlencode "token=$RAMP_API_TOKEN"
155: ```
156: ## Error handling
157: ### Token request errors
158: Failed requests to `/developer/v1/token` return HTTP `400` with error code `DEVELOPER_7012` and one of these messages:
159: | Message | What to check |
160: | --- | --- |
161: | Client authentication failed. | Client ID and secret, and the environment |
162: | The provided authorization grant or refresh token is invalid. | The code expired, was already used, or the `redirect_uri` doesn't match; or the refresh token expired or was revoked |
163: | The requested scope is invalid, unknown, malformed, or exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. | Request only scopes configured for your app |
164: | The authenticated client is not authorized to use this authorization grant type. | Enable the grant type in your app settings |
165: If the client credentials are missing or malformed, the request returns HTTP `401`.
166: ### API errors
167: - **401 Unauthorized**: The token is missing, expired, or invalid.
168: - **403 Forbidden**: The token lacks a required scope. For Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI, the user's role doesn't allow the action, or the connection is read-only and the request makes a change (`DEVELOPER_7100`). Some role errors from these tools return `400` with the message `You do not have the required permissions to use this tool`.
169: - **429 Too Many Requests**: See [Rate Limiting](</developer-api/v1/rate-limiting>).
170: ## FAQ
171: ## Need help?
172: [Submit a Developer API support ticket](</developer-api/v1/debugging#how-to-submit-a-developer-api-support-ticket>) and our team will follow up.
173: #### My customer sees "An admin must connect this app." What's wrong?
174: Only an Admin or Business Owner can approve apps that access the whole business. Ask one to complete the authorization.
175: #### Do Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI connections need specific scopes?
176: No. They follow the connecting user's Ramp role and the access level chosen when connecting. To switch between Full access and Read-only, reconnect. See [Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI](<#ramp-mcp-and-ramp-cli>).

1: title: Ramp MCP
2: source_url: /developer-api/v1/ramp-mcp
3: summary: Ramp MCP connects AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor to your Ramp account. Each connection acts as the signed-in user, with that user's Ramp permissions.
4: content:
5: Ramp MCP connects AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor to your Ramp account. Each connection acts as the signed-in user, with that user's Ramp permissions.
6: ## Connect
7: - **Claude:** Install Ramp from [Claude's directory↗](<https://claude.ai/directory/61bac03c-3f98-4b3c-affb-1b99533fa82c>), then sign in to Ramp.
8: - **ChatGPT:** Install Ramp from the [ChatGPT app directory↗](<https://chatgpt.com/apps/ramp/asdk_app_69250fb6281c819195b52a1556b0060c>).
9: - **Cursor:** [Add Ramp to Cursor](<cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=ramp&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL21jcC5yYW1wLmNvbS9tY3AifQ>) with one click.
10: - **Claude Code:**
11: ```bash
12: claude mcp add --transport http ramp https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp
13: ```
14: - **Codex:**
15: ```bash
16: codex mcp add ramp --url https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp
17: ```
18: - **Other clients:** Coding agents can also use [Ramp CLI](</developer-api/v1/cli>). For other MCP clients, gateways, and the sandbox, see [Connect to Ramp↗](<https://agents.ramp.com/docs/guides/connecting>).
19: When you sign in, choose **Full access** or **Read-only**. Connections expire after 30 days; reconnect to renew.
20: ## Connection issues
21: - **"The app you are using is not currently supported"** means your client's redirect URI isn't allowlisted. [Request a redirect URI](</developer-api/v1/mcp-redirect-whitelist-request>).
22: - **You can't connect at all:** your Ramp role may not include access to AI tools. Ask your Admin; see [Manage connected AI tools↗](<https://support.ramp.com/managing-connected-ai-tools>).
23: For the full tool list and more troubleshooting, see [Connect to Ramp↗](<https://agents.ramp.com/docs/guides/connecting>) and the [Agent tools reference↗](<https://agents.ramp.com/docs/reference/agent-tools>).

1: title: Quickstart
2: source_url: /developer-api/v1/getting-started
3: summary: This guide will help you make your first Ramp API call in just a few minutes. You'll create an access token and call the Transactions API to retrieve transaction data.
4: content:
5: This guide will help you make your first Ramp API call in just a few minutes. You'll create an access token and call the Transactions API to retrieve transaction data.
6: This guide assumes you are a Ramp customer with **admin** access to your dashboard. Need a test environment for development? [Request sandbox access](</developer-api/v1/sandbox-access>).
7: - [Need a test environment for development?](</developer-api/v1/sandbox-access>): Request sandbox access
8: ## 1. Create your app and get credentials
9: First, you'll need to create a developer app to get your API credentials.
10: 1. In your Ramp account, go to **Company → Developer** (you'll need admin access).
11: 2. Click **Create New App**.
12: 3. Name your app (e.g., "API Quickstart") and accept the Terms.
13: 4. Under **Grant types**, click **Add new grant type** → select **Client Credentials**.
14: 5. Under **Scopes**, click **Configure allowed scopes** and select `transactions:read`.
15: 6. Copy your **Client ID** and **Client Secret**. Store them securely – you'll need them in the next step.
16: For more details on authorization, see the [Authorization Guide](</developer-api/v1/authorization>).
17: ## 2. Get an access token
18: With your credentials, request an access token. Ramp authenticates this `/developer/v1/token` request with HTTP Basic Auth: base64-encode `client_id:client_secret` and send it in the `Authorization` header. The token authenticates your API requests.
19: Replace `{environment-url}` with:
20: - `https://demo-api.ramp.com` for Sandbox
21: - `https://api.ramp.com` for Production
22: ## API URLs are different from the Ramp app URLs
23: The API base URL is not the same as the URL for the Ramp customer app. Make sure you're pointing your API calls at the API host, not the frontend host.
24: | Environment | API base URL | Ramp app URL |
25: | --- | --- | --- |
26: | Production | `https://api.ramp.com` | `https://app.ramp.com` |
27: | Sandbox (demo) | `https://demo-api.ramp.com` | `https://demo.ramp.com` |
28: ```bash
29: curl -X POST '{environment-url}/developer/v1/token' \
30: -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET" | base64)" \
31: -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
32: -d "grant_type=client_credentials" \
33: -d "scope=transactions:read"
34: ```
35: Response:
36: ```json
37: {
38: "access_token": "ramp_business_tok_abc123...",
39: "token_type": "Bearer",
40: "expires_in": 864000,
41: "scope": "transactions:read"
42: }
43: ```
44: Store the `access_token` securely – you'll use it to make API calls. Run the token request in your backend or local development environment; do not expose the client secret in browser code. Use `expires_in` to determine how long the token is valid, in seconds. Client Credentials access tokens expire after 10 days. Client Credentials grants do not return a refresh token; request a new access token when the current token expires.
45: The `scope` parameter is required for this example. If you omit it from a Client Credentials request, Ramp issues a token with no scopes, which cannot call the Transactions endpoint.
46: ## 3. Make your first API call
47: With your access token, you can now call the Ramp API. Let's retrieve your transactions using the [GET /transactions](</developer-api/v1/api/transactions#get-developer-v1-transactions>) endpoint.
48: Add the header `Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN_HERE>` and make a GET request to `{environment-url}/developer/v1/transactions`.
49: ```bash
50: curl -X GET '{environment-url}/developer/v1/transactions' \
51: -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN"
52: ```

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

You can use a sandbox to test your integration and access test data, and live mode to access actual account data. Each mode has its own set of API keys, and objects in one mode aren’t accessible to the other. For example, a sandbox product object can’t be part of a live mode payment.

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

In a sandbox, card networks and payment providers don’t process payments.API calls return simulated objects. For example, you can retrieve and use test Customer, PaymentIntent, Refund and Subscription objects.Use test credit cards and accounts. You can’t accept real payment methods or work with real accounts.Identity doesn’t perform any verification checks. Also, Connect account objects don’t return sensitive fields.

In live mode, card networks and payment providers do process payments.API calls return real objects. For example, you can retrieve and use real Customer, PaymentIntent, Refund and Subscription objects.Accept real credit cards and work with customer accounts. candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

Stripe provides a set of default rules when you create your first agent-tagged key. These rules cover high-risk actions such as payouts, refunds and account configuration changes.

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: This is the recommended way to give autonomous agents access to your Stripe account. The approval rules act as a safeguard against agent mistakes, unexpected behaviour and hallucinations – giving you visibility and control without blocking agents from doing their jobs.

evidence.observation: quote: API protocols and headers

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: The Plaid API is JSON over HTTP. Requests are POST requests, and responses are JSON, with errors indicated in response bodies as error_code and error_type (use these in preference to HTTP status codes for identifying application-level errors). All responses come as standard JSON, with a small subset returning binary data where appropriate. The Plaid API is served over HTTPS TLS v1.2 to ensure data privacy; HTTP and HTTPS with TLS versions other than 1.2 are not supported. Clients must use an up to date root certificate bundle as the only TLS verification path; certificate pinning should never be used. All requests must include a Content-Type of application/json and the body must be valid JSON.

For example, Sandbox does not reflect institution-specific transaction history limits, and institutions that do not return pending transactions in Production may return pending transactions in Sandbox. candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: Sandbox data is not always based on a consistent data source across different API calls, especially across different products. For example, Sandbox transaction history may show income and outflow inconsistent with the balance shown on the account, and some products, like Signal, generate random results in Sandbox. Triggering a transfer using a Transfer endpoint will not cause that transaction to show up when calling /transactions/sync or change the balance of the account when calling /accounts/balance/get. Sandbox Profiles and custom test data give you a consistent data source across products when you need one.

evidence.observation: quote: You will incur charges for one-time fee products whenever the product is successfully added to an Item. This occurs when an Item has been successfully created by Link and this product was specified in /link/token/create. An Item is typically considered to be successfully created if a public_token was exchanged, but sometimes (e.g. when using micro-deposit Auth flows, or the in-Link Identity Match flow) it may be considered created once the public_token was created. evidence.observation: quote: prompt is an optional parameter on the authorization request — the /v1/authorize URL you send the user to, not your redirect URI. It controls which screens a user sees when they already have a Brex session or an existing grant. Values are space-delimited, and Brex supports two of the values defined in 3.1.2.1. Authentication Request:

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: We recommend sending prompt=consent. The consent screen is where a user who can reach more than one Brex account chooses which account to connect; for example, an external firm like an accountant or bookkeeper can pick between the client accounts they operate on behalf of. Without forcing a selection, the OAuth authorization request would silently skip that screen and the user's primary account may be selected for them. See which account a token represents.

candidate_excerpts.warning: Candidate excerpt only; do not promote automatically

evidence.observation: quote: Send prompt=login when users of your application may have multiple Brex logins, to force re-authentication so they sign in as the login they mean to connect rather than whoever an active session belongs to. This is a separate concern from account selection: login decides which user signs in, consent decides which of that user's accounts you connect to. You can send both.
